Subject: Control/Data Plane Segregation for Private VPC - management adapter & egress mapping

Hi Mike / Lauren,

Thanks again for the time today. As discussed, ACME wants a short written readout for the private VPC deployment showing how the Redwood control plane management traffic will be segregated from customer inference data paths, and how egress (telemetry, telemetry proxies, and optional fallback) will be handled to meet your compliance constraints.

Attached: a working adapter diagram we sketched (private-vpc-adapter-diagram-v3.pdf) and a draft egress policy spreadsheet. We need your team to confirm:
- Which subnets are allowed to peer with Redwood management endpoints (CIDR /32s or VPC peering ranges)
- Whether NAT/Gateway-based egress is acceptable for telemetry, or you require direct peering to a telemetry ingest endpoint
- KMS/HSM key management preferences and any HSM attestation requirements for key import

Agenda for the technical review call I propose next week: 1) control-plane peering options, 2) data-plane isolation and routing, 3) egress firewall matrix and retention windows, 4) acceptance checklist for SOC2 evidence.

Ben / team,

Thanks — received the diagram and matrix. Quick notes from our side:
- ACME prefers control-plane management traffic to be brought over a dedicated VPC peering session (no public NAT) — management CIDRs will be 10.40.1.0/24 and 10.40.2.0/24.
- Telemetry: we cannot allow inference payloads to exit to the public internet. Telemetry (metrics only) can be sent to a collector in our monitoring VPC via an internal NLB; TLS mutual auth is required.
- KMS: we have an HSM-backed Cloud KMS; Redwood must support wrapping keys with our KMS key and rotation signatures for audits.

I attached ACME's SOC2 evidence bundle (acme-soc2-evidence.zip) for what the audit team expects. Also uploaded an internal diagram that shows the required egress tap point.

We can do the review on Thursday 11th at 10:00 PT. Please confirm attendees.

-Mike

Subject: Re: Control/Data Plane Segregation for Private VPC - management adapter & egress mapping

Ben / Mike / team,

Appreciate the clear asks — a few technical clarifications and a proposed acceptance checklist:

1) Peering model: agree with dedicated VPC peering for management. We will terminate control-plane API endpoints in a management subnet that only accepts traffic from the ACME management CIDRs. No public IPs for control-plane ingress.

2) Telemetry path: implementing an internal-only telemetry sink via mTLS to your NLB is straightforward. We'll add an option to route metrics over the peering link on a separate port (9411 for tracing, 9090 for prometheus) and will ensure no payloads containing PII leave the VPC.

3) Data plane isolation: inference nodes will keep payloads on the customer's VPC. Our runtime agent (the node-side adapter) will implement a local egress policy forbidding outbound HTTP/HTTPS except to the approved telemetry NLB and our management CIDRs. That adapter will run as a daemonset with policy enforced by iptables and an audited startup config.

4) KMS/HSM: we support envelope encryption where Redwood holds a data key encrypted by customer's KMS key. For HSM attestations we can include a signed key-wrap proof in the provisioning API — need to confirm ACME's expected signature format.

Proposed acceptance checklist (we should capture in the runbook):
- Control-plane only reachable from ACME management CIDRs (test: tcp/443 handshake from 10.40.1.5)
- Telemetry delivered to ACME NLB with mTLS (test: prometheus scrape over peering)
- No outbound inference payloads to public internet (test: egress attempt blocked)
- KMS key-wrap proof verifiable by ACME (test: signed artefact in provisioning response)

I can make these items as automated checks in the post-deploy acceptance script. If we agree, I will update the diagram and the egress-policy-matrix.xlsx accordingly and post a version with specific port and CIDR rows.

Irene Choi
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — good alignment. Quick summary and next steps before Thursday's call:

Summary:
- ACME requires dedicated peering for control-plane management (ACME CIDRs: 10.40.1.0/24, 10.40.2.0/24).
- Telemetry must flow to ACME's internal NLB via mTLS; no inference payloads to public internet.
- HSM-backed KMS wrap supported; Redwood will produce key-wrap proofs for provisioning.
- Acceptance checklist (Irene's itemized tests) will be added to the deployment runbook.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Irene: update diagram + egress-policy-matrix with ports/CIDRs and produce acceptance-script snippets (ETA: Wed EOD PT).
- Soojin: prepare a short ops playbook for peering cutover and rollback steps (ETA: Thu morning).
- Jonas: confirm monitoring retention/forwarding limits and whether we need a separate telemetry VPC (ETA: Thu afternoon).
- ACME (Lauren/Mike): confirm Thursday 11:00-11:30 PT works and share any sample certs for mTLS testing ahead of time.

We will treat the Thursday call as the runbook/acceptance signoff. If ACME approves the acceptance checklist there, we can schedule the staging cutover next week.
